title: Jubilee Vessel of Pepi I
image_changes: None; museum JPEG reproduced unchanged. The Walters Art Museum, CC0.
text_changes: Museum inscription field separated into translation, transcription and alternative rendering; wording preserved, HTML whitespace normalized. Longer description excluded.

passages.text: The Horus, Mery-tawy (Beloved of the Two Lands); King of Upper and Lower Egypt, Mery-re (Beloved of Re); First occasion of the Sed-festival; Given life and dominion forever, given life and dominion forever
passages.remark: Alternative museum rendering of the same inscription: Right column: "First of the Sed Festival" Middle column: "King of Upper and Lower Egypt", Mery-Ra Left column: "Horus name=Mery-tawy"; Horizontally " Given life and happiness forever" (this twice)

note: The museum inscription field renders all three labelled columns and the repeated horizontal blessing. Its second rendering is preserved as an alternative, not counted as another inscription. AncientLens scholarly review: unreviewed. Egypt, Saqqara (Place of Origin); Egypt (Place of Discovery). passages.text: Farewell Aurelia Artemis, Pasion’s daughter, incomparably sweetest among all.

note: The museum supplies the Greek epitaph and its corresponding English rendering; the photograph shows the four-line epitaph below the figure. title: Foundation Tablet
image_changes: None; museum composite JPEG reproduced unchanged. The Walters Art Museum, CC0.
text_changes: Translation labels removed; face labels, wording and slash-separated lines preserved. Longer description excluded.

passages.text: on obverse: (For) Utu, / lord of justice of heaven and earth, / learned in decision, / the one who choses in favor of innocence, / the king of Ebabbar, / his king, / Sin-iddinam, / the shepherd who decorates everything / for Nippur, / the provider of Ur, / king of Larsa, / king of Sumer and Akkad, / the Ebabbar, / his beloved house,; On reverse: for the sake of his life, / he built (it) / For abundant distant days / he enlarged that dwelling place. / With the thing that he (Sin-iddinam) has done, / (may) Utu, / rejoice. / A life of sweet things / (and) bright days / as a reward, / may he (Utu) give to him (Sin-iddinam).
passages.remark: The museum does not specify the ancient language. Its current date is retained; older mirrored metadata may use a different chronology.

note: The museum explicitly describes an inscription on two faces and publishes labelled obverse and reverse translations, including the final blessing. Both are reproduced together without omission. AncientLens scholarly review: unreviewed. Mesopotamia (Place of Origin); exact findspot not supplied.
